chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about gold and silver: 'What is the minimum on which zakat is due?' He said: 'Two hundred dirhams, and its equivalent from gold.' He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about the small change — the five and the ten. He said: 'There is nothing due on it until it reaches forty, then one dirham is given for every forty dirhams.'

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمُ: dirham — unit of silver currency used in early Islamic financial jurisprudence
key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: zakat — obligatory alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.النَّيِّفُ: nayif — small excess or fractional amount above a round number, exempt from additional zakat
key_terms.النِّصَابُ: nisab — the minimum threshold of wealth above which zakat becomes obligatory

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of silver and gold on which zakat is due according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the nisab (minimum threshold) for zakat on silver and gold: 200 dirhams for silver and the equivalent value in gold. It also clarifies that fractional amounts below the next increment of forty are exempt — nothing is due until the next full forty dirhams is reached, after which one dirham is owed per forty. This ruling, delivered by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in response to direct inquiry, addresses practical questions faced by merchants and landholders in early Islamic society, ensuring precision in fulfilling zakat as one of the five pillars of Islam.
